headline: Highest risk is medium: Copilot can write and modify repo state while LlamaFactory is read-only, so prompt-injection and data-leakage paths are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible bridge exists through manual copy/paste or shared editor buffers: agent_a reads and writes repo context, while agent_b has no file or network surfaces, so it cannot autonomously inject back. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is limited to unusual operator-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or buffers
IF both agents are pointed at the same editable workspace through the editor
mitigations: Keep agent_b isolated from any copied code or prompts from agent_a
Disable copy/paste of agent_a outputs into agent_b sessions
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Review any pasted content before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read repo context and write edits, but agent_b has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no files or secrets surfaces. That makes cross-agent leakage unlikely except through manual transfer of content by the operator, with small blast radius limited to the visible editor buffers.
conditions: IF the operator shares agent_a editor buffers with agent_b
IF sensitive source code is present in the repo context shown to agent_a
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in repo context
Run agent_b on sanitized prompts only
Use separate accounts or sessions for each agent
Redact sensitive snippets before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write files and modify git state, while agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, or access the filesystem. Because only one agent has mutable repo capabilities, there is no meaningful write-write conflict; any overlap is read-only or operator-mediated.
conditions: IF agent_b is replaced with a writable tool or shell-enabled agent
IF the operator manually applies agent_b suggestions into the same git branch
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only
Require human review before applying agent_a edits
Use branch protection for git changes
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces code edits and repo-aware suggestions that a human may pass into agent_b, but agent_b has no built-in verification or action-taking surfaces documented here. The main risk is that agent_b could echo or reframe agent_a output as support text without checking it, creating a default-path cascade through operator workflow.
conditions: IF agent_b is prompted with agent_a-generated code or claims
IF the operator treats agent_b output as authoritative without review
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require agent_b to cite source lines before restating claims
Use a checklist for any code or policy advice passed onward
Limit agent_a output to diffs, not prose

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for agent_b, while agent_a is a GitHub-hosted closed-source service handling repo context. The only concrete compliance concern is ordinary source-code handling, so this is lower severity and does not implicate agent_b with a distinct regulated-data regime.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the repo context
IF organizational policy forbids sending source code to a vendor-hosted coding assistant
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo context
Confirm vendor data-processing terms before use
Restrict agent_a to non-sensitive repositories
Document retention expectations for code prompts
